literal: Even if you do disgraceful and painful things, to those who are intoxicated, like liquor indeed is, O deceiver, your chest.
translation: O deceiver! Even if you do disgraceful and painful things to me, your chest is like liquor to those who are already intoxicated by it.
modern: கள்வனே! நீ அவமானப்படத்தக்க துன்பங்களைச் செய்தாலும், உன்னால் மயங்கியவர்களுக்கு உன்னுடைய மார்பு மதுவைப் போன்றதே ஆகும்.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine addresses her lover as a deceiver or rogue (கள்வ) because of his hurtful behavior. She explains that even when he causes her shameful distress (இளித்தக்க இன்னா செயினும்), she cannot stay away from him. His chest or embrace (மார்பு) acts like liquor (கள்) to an addict (களித்தார்க்கு). Just as a drunkard craves more alcohol despite the harm it causes, she yearns for his embrace despite the pain he inflicts.
